requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.references.util`.

**Obligations and the tests that check them**

1. **The built-in `habeas:util` exists with the stated text.**
   - `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` resolves `habeas:util`. It asserts the text starts with "Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside" and ends with "judges what it does as part of that root."
   - The same test asserts the full text equals the block quote in `md/reference.md`, using `quoted_text`. That is the documentation the built-in requirement calls for.
   - The test does not compare the middle of the text with the requirement's own quote. The middle is pinned only through `md/reference.md`. I judged this acceptable because the documentation quote and the requirement quote read identically.
   - It also asserts that `habeas:none` and `habeas:other` are not built-ins, and that `is_builtin_name` accepts and rejects the right strings.

2. **Only `{cite}` may reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary.**
   - The `src/builtins.rs` test asserts `check(Cite)` is ok. It asserts `check(Impl)` and `check(Test)` fail with "built-in habeas:util may only be referenced with {cite}".
   - `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` covers an inline citation, a fenced citation with commentary, and a fenced citation with no commentary (`inline`, `fenced`, `bare`). It also checks that `{impl}` and `{test}` references to `habeas:util` produce the "may only be referenced with {cite}" error at the expected lines.
   - `fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` checks the same through a wrong-role fenced reference. It also shows that unknown names such as `habeas:other` are rejected.

3. **An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` needs no citation review.**
   - The `habeas_util_citations_cover…` test asserts there is no "missing citation review" for `inline`, `fenced` or `bare`.
   - The `fenced_references_in_comments…` test asserts the same for `glue`.
   - The `mixed` item also cites `rules.ready`, and the test asserts it still needs a review. This confirms the exemption applies only when `habeas:util` is the item's sole citation.

4. **A citation of `habeas:util` covers its item under `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.**
   - The `habeas_util_citations_cover…` test asserts no "function inline/fenced/bare" coverage error.
   - The `fenced_references_in_comments…` test asserts none for `glue` or `empty`.
   - The wrong-role items `implemented` and `tested` are reported as having no recent coverage. This shows that only a valid citation covers the item.

5. **Built-ins need no evidence.** Both tests assert that no `evidence/habeas:` error appears.

No gaps were found, and no acknowledgments were needed.

text: :::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins themselves MUST NOT require or permit
definition evidence files and MUST NOT appear as definitions in the requirements
index, `habeas status`, or the missing-evidence check of
{cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. Per-source citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` MAY be required for references
to a built-in. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
